title: Benchmark-driven sampling and priority curation for performance advisory requests
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a high volume of non-bug optimization/advisory requests (batching/caching knob tuning, quantization profile requests, routing policy adjustments). Our current intake surface returns long queues and inconsistent prioritization: tickets with similar business impact are treated inconsistently, and many requests lack representative sample workloads, making engineering investigations expensive and slow. We need a reproducible, telemetry-driven approach to surface high-value requests, reduce per-request effort, and provide consistent SLAs for enterprise customers.

Goals: (1) Create a benchmark-driven sampling layer that automatically selects representative request payloads and traffic slices for each advisory intake; (2) Define a transparent priority curation rubric that combines SLO impact, customer cost sensitivity, potential unit-cost delta, and rollout risk; (3) Integrate sampling and prioritization into the intake UI so PMs/SEs can quickly approve a standardized investigation bundle; (4) Reduce average TTR (time to recommendation) for high-priority advisory requests by 40% by end of cycle.
proposal:
Overview: Build an automated sampling & scoring pipeline that enriches inbound advisory tickets with (a) a small set of sanitized representative payloads (3–10 samples), (b) measured latency/cost percentile deltas from recent traces, and (c) a computed priority score. Priority score formula (initial iteration): Priority = 0.4 * SLO_Risk + 0.25 * Cost_Leverage + 0.2 * Customer_Sensitivity + 0.15 * Operational_Risk. Components: 
- SLO_Risk: computed from recent 7d trace anomalies and customer SLA tier (0–100).
- Cost_Leverage: estimated per-token unit cost delta if suggested knob applied (normalized 0–100).
- Customer_Sensitivity: explicit enterprise flags (billing, legal, revenue-impact) and customer-reported severity.
- Operational_Risk: rollout complexity and rollback exposure.

Sampling: Use rolling N quantile sampling across the customer’s recent request histogram (latency & sequence length) + prefix grouping for chat flows to capture KV cache warm/cold states. Samples are sanitized (PII redaction) and packaged with a small runbook for reproducibility (model, seq_len, temperature, routing policy).

UI/Workflow: Intake form auto-attaches the package; PM/SE can preview sample set and accept/replace. Tickets with score >= 75 are routed to the Optimization Rapid Queue (SLA: 3 business days for investigation bundle). Scores 50–74 go to Standard Advisory (SLA: 10 business days). Below 50 require manual triage and justification.

Engineering integration: Provide an API endpoint that returns sample bundles and score metadata. Add a lightweight console panel for reviewers showing the score breakdown and suggested initial knobs (batch size, cache TTL, quant profile). All suggested knobs link to a feature-flagged runtime test harness for quick validation on dedicated playground infra.
acceptance_criteria: Automated sampling pipeline produces a sanitized sample bundle for >= 90% of incoming advisory tickets in QA environment
Priority score computed and attached to each new advisory ticket with visible score breakdown in console
Routing rules automatically route tickets with score >=75 to Optimization Rapid Queue and create downstream investigation tasks
PM/SE reviewer can accept or swap samples and trigger a quick-run validation in the test harness
Average time from ticket create -> first investigation artifact (bench results or knob recommendation) reduced by 40% for tickets routed to Rapid Queue in pilot customers
tasks: Design sampling algorithm and define 5 canonical sampling heuristics (seq_len quantiles, KV cache states, prompt prefixes)
Implement backend service to assemble sanitized sample bundles and compute priority score
Add intake UI changes: sample preview, score breakdown, accept/replace controls
Create routing rules and Automation: Rapid Queue workflow + SLA enforcement
Build small runtime test harness on dedicated infra and wire quick-run endpoint
Create docs: reviewer playbook, knob suggestion mapping, and privacy redaction guidelines
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers and collect feedback/metrics
stakeholders: Customer Success: Leah Nguyen and Rajiv Menon
metrics: TTR (time-to-recommendation) for tickets in Rapid Queue — target -40%
% of tickets with valid sample bundles produced — target >=90%
Number of knob suggestions validated in test harness per week
Customer satisfaction (CSAT) for advisory engagements — improvement target +0.2
risks: Sanitization gaps could leak PII — mitigation: strict redaction library and manual audit for pilot
Score gaming by customers or internal bias — mitigation: make score features auditable and allow override with justification
Sampling not representative for low-volume customers — mitigation: fallback to synthetic strain tests + requestor-provided sample
Test-harness resource contention — mitigation: quota + feature flag controlling concurrency
